content.intro: In this lesson, focus on trying tailwind css without a build setup and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to trying tailwind css without a build setup, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Create a minimal example demonstrating trying tailwind css without a build setup. Include a before/after comparison and explain why the chosen utility, variant or directive is appropriate.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to trying tailwind css without a build setup.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to trying tailwind css without a build setup.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.

content.expected_output: The experiment demonstrates syntax quickly; production CSS should come from a supported build workflow.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying trying tailwind css without a build setup without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Trying Tailwind CSS Without a Build Setup is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
